equivalents.note: The Tibetan reads 'in the middle of the town' where the Bengali has the obscure ṭālata; the comment (cp.33.m2) cites the same phrase but transliterates Munidatta's ṭā and ṭamāla as DA and DA ma la.
The line has khru ba (normally 'cubit'), apparently for phru ba, 'earthen pot', which the comment (cp.33.m2) has.
zan is food in general (porridge, dough) rather than boiled rice in particular; the comment (cp.33.m2) has the same word.
The Tibetan line has sbrul, 'snake', where Shastri's Bengali prints saṃsāra, supporting the snake that Munidatta's sayaḥ (cp.33.m3) implies.
The Tibetan has intransitive skyes gyur pa, 'came to birth, arose', which leaves open whether the ox gives birth or is itself born.
The comment (cp.33.m4) cites glang but treats Munidatta's bala as a loanword, ba la, glossed 'flesh' (sha).
The Tibetan has 'bri, 'female yak', as if piṭā named the animal being milked, and the comment (cp.33.m4) keeps 'bri where Munidatta has pīṭhaka, 'stool'.
The line sets blo ldan, 'having understanding', against blo med pa, 'without understanding', for the two budhī; the comment (cp.33.m5) has plain blo for Munidatta's buddhi.
chom po, 'robber, bandit', recurs in the comment (cp.33.m5) for the king of mind, unlike the rkun ma and rkun po used for the thief of song 2.
The Tibetan has bla ma'i drin, 'the guru's kindness', here and in cp.33.m4, with no word for lineage or transmission.
The Tibetan has rdo rje'i rtsa ba nas, 'from the root of the vajra', making the root the starting point of the movement to the wheel of great bliss rather than a gloss on the teat.
The comment cites ba, 'cow', for Munidatta's gāvī; the verse line (cp.33.3a) has no separate word for the cow.
The Tibetan has khyim du, 'in the house', making Nairātmā the barren woman in the lord of yogis' house rather than his wife.
The Tibetan has rnam par spyod pa, 'engaging, practising', as if from vi-car 'move, act', where Munidatta's vicāryamāṇa means 'being examined'.
The Tibetan renders caryā here as glu dbyangs, 'song', the word it uses for rāga in the heading (cp.33.h1), not spyod pa, 'conduct'.

questions: cow (cp.33.3a): the Tibetan line has no word for the cow; mo gsham, 'barren female' (already matched for barren), stands for the barren cow, and the pa ni before it may be a slip for ba ni. The equivalent is given from the comment (cp.33.m4, ba).

mana-pavana (cp.33.m4): in the Tibetan of Saraha's verse (rnal 'byor dri med mchog gi bde chen 'gyur) there is no yid dang rlung; dri med mchog, 'stainless, supreme', stands where manapavana is, perhaps from a different reading (pavana taken as 'purifying'?), so no equivalent is given.

paksa (cp.33.m6): the Sanskrit has pakṣi- in the obscure compound pakṣivikṣubdhacitta-, probably not pakṣa 'side'; the Tibetan (sems kyis yongs su rtogs pa nyung ste, rtag tu lta ba'i sems can chen po) has no phyogs or other word for it, so the glossary match looks like a false hit.
samsara (cp.33.m6): the Tibetan has no 'khor ba; de nyid dang bcas pa'i sems stands for sa eva saṃsāra(na)citta-, as if the translators read a sa- 'with' and no saṃsāra, so no equivalent is given.

house (cp.33.m2): marked already matched, but the only khyim in this segment's Tibetan is inside khyim tshes, 'neighbour' (bdag gi khyim tshes su gnas pa zla ba nyi ma): the Tibetan folds Munidatta's mama gṛhaṃ, 'my house', and pārśvastha, 'neighbouring', into 'abiding as my neighbour', so the automatic match there is doubtful.
